content.text: Ritalin, Ritalin SR, Methylin, Metadate ER or CD, Concerta, Daytrana- patch
abrupt d/c -> w.draw sx - taper after chronic use
taper if long ↑dose use - fatigue, depression
+5 mg q wk; +2.5 mg q wk
SWD: 150 mg ~1 h b4 work shift
peds <70 kg: 0.5 mg/kg/day; peds ±70 kg/adults: 40 mg/day
: block presynaptic DA and NE reuptake; amphetamines also increase DA release; inhibit MAO
•psychiatric – psychosis, mood disturb, severe anxiety or panic attacks
•⍉in pts w/ known ♡ abnormalities ← ↑risk of sudden death – specifically, some agents are CI in pts w/ HF, recent MI, arrhythmia, or mod-severe HTN
•most stimulants are CI in pts w/ marked anxiety, tension, agitation, glaucoma, hyperthyroidism, or hx of a tic dx
: CNS stimulants, incl amphetamine ER oral formulations, other amphetamine-containing prod, and methylphenidate, have a ↑potential for abuse and dependence
: misuse may cause sudden death & serious CV events
: severe CV events & other vasc problems, increase suicidality, exacerbate pre-existing psychiatric disorders, seizures, stunted growth, serotonin syndrome

content.text: -    Note: valproic acid (Depakene) = same valproate family as divalproex (see Divalproex)
-    MOA: ↑GABA (⍉ GABA-transaminase -> ↑[GABA]) + block Na+/T-type Ca2+ channels -> ↓neuronal excitability
-    Caution: ⍉ hepatic dz, POLG mitochondrial dx, urea cycle dx    -    preg — ⍉unless others failed (effective contraception)
-    Monitoring: serum levels — mania 50-125 mcg/mL, epilepsy 50-100    -    LFTs prior + frequently (esp first 6 mo)    -    CBC/PLT (thrombocytopenia ↑ @ ≥110 F / ≥135 M)
-    BBW: hepatotoxicity (USU first 6 mo; <2y highest risk)    -    pancreatitis    -    fetal risk (NTD, ↓IQ, neurodevelopmental dx)
-    BBW: SJS/TEN (screen HLA-B*1502 in Asian-ancestry pts)    -    aplastic anemia/agranulocytosis

content.text: ER QD = 8-20% higher dose than IR total daily; mania trough target 85-125 mcg/mL
AEDs: do ⍉ abruptly d/c (status epilepticus risk)
•Tx both mania & depression w/o inducing either state
•can induce manic episodes & cycling freq; only used as adjunct therapy to a mood stabilizer
•anti-mania; adjunct agents for short-term use only

: several proposed mechanisms, may be related to lithium’s ability to inhibit excitatory NT (DA, NE) funct &/or funct of membrane-bound enzymes that activate second messengers (↑activity during mania)
: GI (nausea, loose stools), polyuria, polydipsia, fine hand tremor, musc weakness
•chronic tx: nephrogenic DI, hypothyroidism, wt gain, edema, chronic interstitial nephritis, minimal Δ glomerulopathy
: serum lithium levels should be monitored to ⍉toxicity
•long term – wt gain, fine hand tremor, PCOS, alopecia, hyperammonemia
: inhibits release of glutamate (an excitatory AA) and inhibits voltage-sensitive sodium channels, which stabilizes neuronal membranes
: ineffective for acute mania – better for pts w/ more depression
: rash, dry mouth, itching, SJS/TEN, aseptic meningitis, DRESS
: in addition to antiseizure effects, carbamazepine has anticholinergic, antineuralgic, antidiuretic, musc relaxant, antimanic, antidepressive, and antiarrhythmic properties
•MC – CNS effects (sedation), dizziness, blurred vision, rash, GI disturb
•hematological effects – transient leukopenia, myelosuppression, agranulocytosis, aplastic anemia
